subject: Mental Models
title: Analogy Stress-Testing
description: Learn Analogy Stress-Testing in one minute.

hook.text: A CEO said 'our company is a family.' Then she fired 200 people. Families don't fire members.

buildup.text: Every analogy has a breaking point where the comparison no longer holds.

discovery.text: Stress-testing an analogy means asking: where does this comparison fail? What is different between the two situations?

twist.text: Bad analogies are not just useless—they are dangerous. They carry hidden assumptions that drive wrong decisions.

climax.text: Use every analogy but also break it. List three ways the comparison fails. That shows you the limits of the insight.

punchline.text: Every analogy breaks somewhere. Find the crack before it matters.

quiz.question: Why should you stress-test analogies?
options: Finding where the comparison fails reveals hidden assumptions and limits
